title.narrative: TEENAGE MOTHERS AND CHILD SUPPORT FOUNDA

description.narrative: According to the report from DHS 2016, Busoga subregion in Eastern Uganda had the highest rate of teenage pregnancy and its associated effects.The research conducted between 2019 and 2020 indicates that Busoga registered as many as 89,347 teenage pregnancies.Busoga tops teenage pregnancies – survey - Daily Monitor Respectively. (https://www.monitor.co.ug ). Teenage mothers face economic hardships as result of sexual and reproductive health rights abuse which in turn leave effects such as high rates of school drop outs, denial of normal child growth, depression, social misfit followed by poverty, hence high levels of poverty in the region. A comprehensive strategy for economic empowerment, capacity building of the victims and psychosocial support services is required to prevent difficulties commonly experienced by young mothers, whose rights have been abused, mentally and physically violated. We intend to mapout a team of young people (teenagers) within the area of operation whose capacity will be built to facilitate extention of economic, social and mental health interventions. TMCSF community offices in Jinja will be used as a distribution center for support services such as  Access to extended economic empowerment services  Weekly group sessions to include; urban farming  Peer social support Network. Topics of discussion will vary from nutrition, mental health issues, and skills training, to education. The project Solidarity with teenage mothers (SWEET) seeks to ensure that a community led model, facilitated by TMCSF, her partners and all community stakeholders create an environment to empower the survivors in skilling and livelihood opportunities, offer social support services. . This is premised on the circumstances through which thesegirls are victimized, defiled and their rights violated. Teenage pregnancies is greatly associated with extreme poverty early and forced marriages,<(>,<)> low educational levels, , inadequate knowledge on sexual and reproductive health information, limitedaccess to affordable contraceptive options, increased HIV/Aids exposure and other poor life style outcomes in children such nutritional deficiencies. The main objective The main objective is to economically socially and mentally empower teenage mothers. With livelihood skill and social services.

participating-org.narrative:
Teenage Mothers and Child Support Foundation (TMCSF) was founded to address the exponentially persistent and increasing girl child abuse, mitigate teenage pregnancies and its related negative consequences. Its founding dates back as early as 2012, Inspiration of one, Mr. Mayanja Josh, now the Executive Director, having been raised by a teenage mother and following the challenges that his mother went through as a child raising a baby who is currently Mr. Mayanja Josh. It is highly believed that the traumaand torments that Josh’s mother under went were witnessed by him in his early stages of growth, thus explaining the passion he has for victims of teenage pregnancy. It’s against this background that Mr. Mayanja Josh, felt should start an organization to intervene in the ever increasing girl child rights abuse. Stages. Teenage Mothers and Child Support Foundation was registered as a CBO, in 2012, then elevated to NGO, operating in Wakiso district and Now has extended to Busoga Sub-region, particularly Jinja and Kamuli District. The organization at the moment is mandated to operate in Wakiso, Jinja and Kamuli. When TMCSF was a CBO, its mandated operational area was Kira Municipality, Bweyogerere division. Its concentration was more of charity, partneredwith churches and mosques to solicit clothes and food which was always given to victims of teenage pregnancy, TMCSF worked with churches also to find families which could temporallyhost victims of teenage pregnancy before being re integrated. By 2015, TMCSF considering the degree of girl child abuse, vulnerability and increase of cases of teenage pregnancy felt it was important, to widen its contextual and geographical scope, hence a need to register as an NGO operating beyond the reach of CBO. TMCSF wasthen registered as an NGO on 19th November 2015 with registration number S.5914/12113 to ensure the rights and dignity of the girl child are respected, address the highly vulnerable and underserved girls who were either pregnant, or had given birth and those raising a child (ren). Even after rolling out such interventions, TMSCF realized that it had not made any significant improvement, since the perpetrators of teenage pregnancy had not been involved. Therefore, a new approach was adopted which wasto include school going boys and male change advocates in the sensitization campaign which has since caused awareness and capacity building amongst teenage girls. There is increased referral of victims of teenage pregnancy, TMCSF has promoted skillingintailoring and here dressing. - TMCSF has empowered over 450 young mothers with vocational practical skills in tailoring and hairdressing that is enabling them have an economic base (small <(>&<)> medium enterprises) to provide for their babies and families, and380 have been certified with National Industrial Training Certificates (UBTEB). - TMCSF successfully referred 280 Teenage mothers through the social support networks to other service providers. - TMCSF also re-integrate 60 teenage mothers into their families and communities after giving birth from safe secured environment - TMCSF signed memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Busoga Kingdom thus enhancing the organization mandate to address teenage pregnancy challenges in the region.
The principalchanges that the organization wants to achieve over a long time include; - To protect the rights of teenage mother’s at risk by ensuring that they have access to facilities such as medical care, education, nutrition, and other basics. - To buildcapacityof a girl child, teenage girl, teenage mothers and other support structures for demand and realization their rights - To empower teenage mothers with agricultural and livelihood skills to increase their income and enable them meet their needs with thoseof their babies - To re-integrate teenage mothers into their families and communities for support

comment.narrative: Through TMSCF identified ambassadors to the teenage mothers (a total of 8 volunteering ambassadors) , the groups have found safe meeting points in their localities especially churches, mosques and town halls including football pitches where they connected to hold their group discussions and share challenges and implement their ideas.

comment.narrative: TMSCF grouped the rightsholders into four groups of 29 per group that made a total of 100 rightsholders. During the implementation of the activities, the project attracted high demand that it exceeded the target number of 100 rightsholders and got an additional number of 15. These were accompanied by the local leaders support. In total 115 rightsholders were reached. The formed groups had a goal of benefiting and accessing available government initiative programs such as the Parish Development Model and Mwoga.

description.narrative: % rightsholder groups indicating increased confidence to raise their voice

comment.narrative: Under TMSCF mentorship program, they focused on building self confidence among the rightsholders. In the quest for this, TMSCF actively involved the rightsholders in co- creation meetings during the Voice grantees communities of practice (COPs) for the community engagement. Case in point is a meeting that was held at Nsambya Cardinal Nsubuga Hotel were TMSCF invited a 16 year old teenage mother who together with her 3 colleagues were able to confidently share their opinions and insights towards the Rightsholders Guiding Tool that was being developed and eventually produced by community engagement COP group of grantees.
